items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'Plot twist' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. 'It never happened.' is delivered slowly and dryly, like a punchline, after a tiny pause. 'to eight.' lands as its own proud beat. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Say U.S.A. as the three letters U-S-A. Pronounce 'Arusha' as 'ah-ROO-shah', 'Kinshasa' as 'kin-SHAH-sah', 'Nairobi' as 'nye-ROH-bee'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word, every line in order; never add words of your own.
lines: Narrator
What if East Africa... became one country?
Narrator
Plot twist: they're drafting the constitution right now.
Narrator
Eight countries, from the Congo... to Somalia.
Narrator
One goal: the East African Federation.
Narrator
So what would this country get?
Narrator
Over three hundred thirty million people... almost as many as the U.S.A.
Narrator
The seventh biggest country on Earth: bigger than India.
Narrator
Africa's highest mountain... its biggest lake... and coasts on two oceans.
Narrator
And they already tried. In nineteen sixty-three, three leaders promised a federation...
Narrator
within the year. It never happened.
Narrator
Their first union collapsed in nineteen seventy-seven.
Narrator
It came back in two thousand... and grew from three countries to eight.
Narrator
But that's not even the weirdest part.
Narrator
There's already an East African passport... an anthem... and a parliament.
Narrator
And the capital? Probably Arusha, in Tanzania.
Narrator
Not Nairobi. Not Kinshasa, the biggest city.
Narrator
And Arusha has just one thing to say.
Narrator
So... one East Africa, or eight countries? Because honestly...
